name: Intraday calm-window drift — low-vol seasonality reversion (15m)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM: vol clustering is real but weak (GARCH/realized-EGARCH 2025 explains <=15% of BTC variance) and, critically, PARTIALLY DETERMINISTIC by clock — crypto realized vol has a persistent intraday shape tied to US/Asia session overlaps and the funding-settlement clock. We trade the seasonal calm windows: when vol_realized and atr are in their low intraday band, mean-reversion/carry drift is cleanest and fee drag is survivable; we AVOID the high-vol session windows where slippage and whipsaw dominate. Entry (long): vol_realized below a fitted ceiling (calm regime) AND atr below a fitted ceiling (low current range) AND range_position below a fitted ceiling (buying the lower half of the calm range, not the top). The other side is not a specific counterparty but a structural inefficiency — most systematic crypto flow ignores intraday seasonality, and the calm-window premium survives because it's un-glamorous and small per-trade. Uses ONLY realized features (no DVOL) so it dodges the 148-point data wall. Exit: atr crosses up through a fitted level (a high-vol window is starting -> get out before the whipsaw) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: the seasonality IS the thesis — if the same edge appears with an hour-of-day / session gate removed (a plain calm-vol reversion, already in the inbox), the intraday-clock claim is unsupported and this collapses into rsi-reversion-calm-vol. DISCONFIRMER 2: <=15% predictable variance means the effect is tiny -> if per-trade net edge doesn't clear ~20bps at 15m it's a fee-eaten curve-fit. DISCONFIRMER 3: session effects can stand in for a few big scheduled events (CPI/FOMC); if excluding those dates kills it, it's event-risk not seasonality.
catalyst: the deterministic low-vol intraday session window where calm drift is cleanest
